questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How delivery apps and 'dark kitchens' change how we eat
How to cook Hawaiian food at home for your family
Why so many restaurants closed during the lockdown
The dangers of delivering food by bike in big cities
questions.why: They discuss the takeaway revolution, delivery-only 'dark kitchens' and their effect on eating.

questions.q: Why is Georgina surprised by Neil's order?
options: It is very expensive for a quick lunch
It is something she has never eaten or even seen
Neil usually cooks all his meals for himself
A poké bowl doesn't sound like typical takeaway food
questions.why: She says, “It doesn't sound like typical takeaway food.”

options: A restaurant that is open only at night
A kitchen that cooks only for delivery, with no diners
An app that connects customers to local takeaways
A kitchen where chefs teach cooking online
questions.why: Neil says they work as just-for-delivery restaurants, without waiters, tables or diners.

questions.q: What do we learn about Anton Soulier?
options: He founded Deliveroo with some friends in 2013
He is a food journalist who writes for the BBC
He runs twelve kitchens in London, Paris and Madrid
He delivers food by bike around central London
questions.why: Georgina says he started Taster and now runs twelve kitchens in London, Paris and Madrid.

questions.q: According to Sheila Dillon, how are the Taster menus designed?
options: So the food stays warm and looks good on arrival
So they can be cooked very quickly by one chef
So they use only fresh, local ingredients
So they are much cheaper than normal restaurants
questions.why: She says they're chosen so they'll be warm, keep their texture and won't look like a dog's dinner.

questions.q: What does Sheila Dillon mean when she says the bike has become a shaper of the foods we eat?
options: Cyclists are now choosing what people order to eat
People are eating much healthier food than before
Bikes are replacing cars for weekly food shopping
Delivery needs now shape which dishes are made
questions.why: The menus are designed to travel well on the back of a bike, so delivery shapes the food.

questions.q: What does Anton Soulier think might happen in twenty or thirty years?
options: Everyone will learn to cook
People might not have kitchens
Restaurants will stop delivering
Delivery will be done by drones
questions.why: He says there is a trend that in twenty, thirty years people might not have kitchens.

questions.q: How does Georgina feel about takeaways compared with cooking?
options: She prefers takeaways and orders one every day
She never eats takeaways because they're unhealthy
She enjoys them sometimes but needs her kitchen
She only cooks at weekends when she has more time
questions.why: She says she enjoys a takeaway sometimes but couldn't survive without her kitchen.
